[[2007 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2007 NCAA Tournament]] }} '''Joshua Scott McRoberts''' (born [[February 28]], [[1987]] in [[Carmel, Indiana]]) was a 6-10 [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]]/[[Center (basketball)|center]] for the [[Duke University]] men's [[basketball]] team during the 2006 and 2007 seasons. McRoberts has declared himself eligible for the [[2007 NBA Draft]], and is projected to be a first-round pick. ==High school career== McRoberts attended [[Carmel High School (Carmel, Indiana)|Carmel High School]] in Carmel, Indiana. McRoberts led the Carmel High School Greyhounds in both scoring and rebounding his senior year. He averaged 17.9 points to go along with 11.4 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 3.0 blocked shots per game and shot an impressive .593 (166-of-280) from the field while guiding the Greyhounds to a 21-4 record and a trip to the sectional championship game in 2005. McRoberts was considered the number one power forward prospect out of high school, and was projected to be drafted in the [[2005 NBA Draft]] had he declared. ==Collegiate career== ===Freshman=== McRoberts averaged 8.7 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.5 assists, and 1.3 blocked shots while leading the team (60.5%) in field goal percentage.{{cite web|title=''Josh McRoberts''|publisher=GoDuke.com|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22727&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=186182&Q_SEASON=2006|accessdate=2007-03-14}} McRoberts was named to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman team. He helped the [[Duke Blue Devils]] to a record of 32-4, the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] regular season title, and the 2006 ACC tournament championship title by defeating the [[Boston College]] Eagles. He was also named to the third team Freshman All-America by collegehoops.net. McRoberts' late-season numbers improved as he recorded 10 of his 15 double-figure scoring games in his final 14 games, while averaging 10.4 points and 6.3 rebounds (with a 59.6 FG%).{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=271339|title=McRoberts Announces Plan To Return For Sophomore Season|publisher=GoDuke.com |date=2006-04-26 |accessdate=2007-01-29}} Considered a potential [[NBA draft]] lottery pick, McRoberts instead stated he would not enter the draft, and would return to Duke for the 2006-2007 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=22724&SPID=1845&DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=271339|title=McRoberts Announces Plan To Return For Sophomore Season|publisher=GoDuke.com |date=2006-04-26 |accessdate=2007-01-29}} McRoberts underwent a successful lumbar [[discectomy]] on August 3rd, 2006. He had been suffering from chronic back problems since high school and had the operation to alleviate the problem. ===Sophomore=== Games 33, PPG: 13.0, RPG: 7.9, APG: 3.5, FG%: 50.2{{cite web|title=''Josh McRoberts''| work=CNNSI.com|url= http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/ncaa/men/players/46499|accessdate=2007-03-18}} On [[December 19]], [[2006]] against [[Kent State University|Kent State]], McRoberts had a career-high 19 points, six blocks, six rebounds, four assists, and four steals making him the first Duke player to tally at least four in all five categories.{{cite web | title= Game Recaps| work= | url= http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/basketball/ncaa/men/recaps/2006/12/19/40577_recap.html| accessdate=2006-12-19}} During the North Carolina game on December 21st, he was seen crying on the bench after Coach Mike Krzyzewski took him out of the game. On [[March 22]], [[2007]] McRoberts declared himself eligible for the [[2007 NBA Draft]].{{cite web | title=''Duke sophomore McRoberts eligible for NBA draft''| work=[[Associated Press]]|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/draft2007/news/story?id=2808295|accessdate=2007-03-22}} ==Awards== ===High School=== {| |valign="top" | *2005 McDonald's All-America Player of the Year *2005 McDonald's All-America Game MVP |valign="top" | *2005 Parade All-America Basketball Team *2005 National High School Coaches Assn.
